note: Rewritten from the species-level description in Sands (1972); original in English; the genus has no soldier caste and only alates and workers are described; measurement tables, figure numbers, type specimens and distribution records are not translated.

sections.label: Diagnostic characters
sections.text: The worker abdomen is probably dehiscent, but in preserved material there are few clear indications. The enteric valve armature, the head pilosity and fontanelle of the alate and even the proportions of the mandibular teeth vary considerably within the species; individual specimens deviate from the main cluster in principal component analysis, almost equidistant from A. cnaphorus, which mainly reflects variation in the mandibular teeth. The available material is not yet sufficient to separate an eastern and a western species on this basis.

sections.label: Worker
sections.text: Head capsule pale yellow, pilosity sparse, yellow. Postclypeus moderately to strongly raised, Pcl/W 0.28–0.35, Pcl/Ri 2.30–3.02. Mandibular apical teeth short, L/L 0.50–0.60, Ra/Rj 0.68–0.80; the accessory marginal tooth of the left mandible is separated from the molar prominence in surface view by a distinct notch, composite ratio 12.52–14.60; the tip of the first marginal tooth of the right mandible is distinctly behind the line from the apical tooth to the second marginal tooth, the anterior margin of the first marginal tooth markedly shorter than that of the second, composite ratio 16.60–18.30. Fore tibia moderately inflated, Ti/Ty 3.58–4.05, the third apical spur small but not vestigial, about one quarter the length of the other two. The midgut-hindgut overlap is four to five and a half times the midgut width at the attachment of the Malpighian tubules; the enteric valve base is very weakly bilobate, connected by a very short neck to the second hindgut pouch, lateral in the undissected abdomen. Enteric valve cushions: cushions 1 and 2 retracted, very small, the surface scaly with only one or two small spines; cushion 3 protruding through the valve opening, cylindrical, tapering towards the apex, bearing 10–15 long slender comb-like spines around its margin, with additional conspicuous spines behind the proximal scales of the cushion; cushion 4 retracted, similar in size to cushion 2, with a scaly surface and one or two small spines; the valve wall bears sparse minute spines between and outside the inner cushions.

sections.label: Alate
sections.text: Head capsule sepia brown, darker above the fontanelle; fontanelle oval to long oval, slightly smaller than the ocellus, slightly concave, yellow; the median spot oval, flat, smaller than the fontanelle, concolorous with the head; postclypeus brown, labrum yellowish brown; frontal mark a flat brown crescent; antennae yellow. Pronotum brown, meso- and metanotal plates yellowish brown, transverse sutures present and weak in some specimens; femora and tibiae yellow, tarsi paler. Abdominal tergites brown, dorsal spiracles sometimes slightly darker, sternites brown laterally together with the ventral spiracles and yellow medially; cerci pale yellow. Posterior margin of head capsule evenly circular; ocelli rather small, separated from the compound eye by one third to four fifths their minimum diameter; postclypeus weakly to moderately raised, Pcl/W 0.23–0.31, posterior margin arched or slightly curved, not evenly circular, median suture usually distinct. Mandibular apical teeth short, La/Li 0.42–0.57, Ra/Ri 0.63–0.74; the accessory marginal tooth of the left mandible just separated from the molar prominence in surface view, composite ratio 8.00–9.30; the apical and marginal teeth of the right mandible are about in the same line, the anterior margins of the first and second marginal teeth equal in length, composite ratio 21.7–29.9. Head capsule pilosity pale yellow, a short fine felt, with erect setae in most specimens, less even in some.
